### noust 2fa

Enrol, confirm, disable or recover two-factor authentication for logins.

```
noust 2fa [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Subcommands: [`backup-codes`](#noust-2fa-backup-codes), [`confirm`](#noust-2fa-confirm), [`disable`](#noust-2fa-disable), [`enroll`](#noust-2fa-enroll), [`status`](#noust-2fa-status)

### noust 2fa backup-codes

Regenerate the backup codes, invalidating every one issued before.

```
noust 2fa backup-codes [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--force` | Do not ask for confirmation. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust 2fa confirm

Verify CODE against the pending secret and activate the second factor.

```
noust 2fa confirm [OPTIONS] CODE
```

Arguments: `code`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust 2fa disable

Turn the second factor off, on presentation of a current CODE or an unused backup code.

```
noust 2fa disable [OPTIONS] CODE
```

Arguments: `code`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust 2fa enroll

Begin enrolment: generate a pending secret. Nothing is enforced until     'noust 2fa confirm CODE' verifies it.

```
noust 2fa enroll [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust 2fa status

Report the two-factor state, without exposing any secret.

```
noust 2fa status [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Print the status as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust access

Roles, and where each person holds them.

```
noust access [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Subcommands: [`grant`](#noust-access-grant), [`list`](#noust-access-list), [`permissions`](#noust-access-permissions), [`revoke`](#noust-access-revoke), [`role`](#noust-access-role)

### noust access grant

Give an account a role at a scope.

```
noust access grant [OPTIONS] USERNAME
```

Arguments: `username`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--role` | A built-in team role or one you defined. |  |
| `--team` | The team. |  |
| `--project` | The project of that team. |  |
| `--env` | The environment of that project. |  |
| `--scope` | Where; the narrowest of --team, --project and --env by default. 'instance' is the whole server (a role you defined, added to the account's own). |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

|---|---|---|

| `--team` | Only what is held in this team. |  |
| `--json` | Print the bindings as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust alert

Alert rules on CPU, memory, disk, load and traffic.

```

```

### noust alert ack

Take an alert that is firing: its reminders stop and the channels are told.

```
noust alert ack [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Arguments: `name`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--app` | The application the alert is about; leave out for the server's. | `` |
| `--by` | Who is taking it, as the channels will say. | `cli` |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |


### noust alert set

Create an alert rule, or replace the one of that name.

```
noust alert set [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Arguments: `name`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--metric` | What to watch. |  |
| `--above` | Fire when it stays above LIMIT (90%, 512MB, 2MB/s). |  |
| `--below` | Fire when it stays below LIMIT. |  |
| `--or-equal` | Count the limit itself as a breach (>= and <=). |  |
| `--for` | How long it must hold before it fires (at least 1m): 5m, 1h. | `5m` |
| `--hysteresis` | How far back inside the limit it must come to clear, in the metric's unit. | `0` |
| `--cooldown` | The least time between two messages about the same thing. | `1h` |
| `--app` | The application, for an application metric (every one by default). |  |
| `--severity` |  | `warning` |
| `--remind` | Say it again every cooldown while it keeps firing. |  |
| `--disabled` | Create it switched off. |  |
| `--note` | Free text for whoever reads the rule later. | `` |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust app adopt

Register a Docker Compose stack that already runs, without touching it.

```
noust app adopt [OPTIONS] DOMAIN
```

Arguments: `domain`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--path` | The directory the stack runs from, such as /opt/proggest. |  |
| `--compose-file` | Its compose file, relative to --path (found among the usual names otherwise). |  |
| `--source` | Where updates fetch from (default: origin). |  |
| `--branch` | The branch updates follow (default: the current). |  |
| `--site` | The site file serving the domain (found by its names otherwise). |  |
| `--port` | The port to register (the compose file's web port otherwise). |  |
| `--accept-recreate` | Adopt even if starting the stack as Noust would recreate something. |  |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Adopt without asking. |  |
| `--json` | Print what was adopted as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust app adopt-site

Register a site that already runs on nginx or Apache, without rebuilding it.

```
noust app adopt-site [OPTIONS] DOMAIN
```

Arguments: `domain`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--site` | The site file serving the domain (found otherwise). |  |
| `--unit` | The unit the site is in front of (the one that listens on its port otherwise). |  |
| `--path` | The directory of its files (the unit's WorkingDirectory or the site's root otherwise). |  |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Adopt without asking. |  |
| `--json` | Print what was adopted as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust app build

The commands an application is installed, built and started with: see, set or unset them.

```
noust app build [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Subcommands: [`set`](#noust-app-build-set), [`show`](#noust-app-build-show), [`unset`](#noust-app-build-unset)

### noust app build set

Set an application's build block, replacing the repository's noust.yaml whole.

```
noust app build set [OPTIONS] DOMAIN
```

Arguments: `domain`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--base-directory` | The subdirectory of the repository the project lives in (apps/web). |  |
| `--install` | Replaces the install command. |  |
| `--build` | Replaces the build command. |  |
| `--start` | Replaces the start command. systemd expands ${PORT}; it is never run by a shell. |  |
| `--publish-directory` | Where a static build leaves the files the web server serves, from the project. |  |
| `--runtime` | Pin the runtime: node@22, python@3.12 or php@8.3. |  |
| `--cache`, `--no-cache` | --no-cache builds every deployment from scratch, without the package managers' cache or the dependencies of the release that serves. |  |
| `--timeout` | How long the install and the build may each take before they are stopped (the server's deploy.install_timeout and deploy.build_timeout otherwise). |  |
| `--file` | Replace the whole block with a YAML file holding 'build:'; '-' reads stdin. |  |
| `--json` | Print the build block now in force as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust app container set

Change how a container application is built and run.

```
noust app container set [OPTIONS] DOMAIN
```

Arguments: `domain`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--image` | Deploy this image from a registry: name[:tag][@sha256:digest]. Needs no source. |  |
| `--builder` | How a repository becomes an image: its Dockerfile, or Railpack, which needs none (noust setup railpack). |  |
| `--dockerfile` | The Dockerfile, relative to the repository. Default: Dockerfile or Containerfile in the context. |  |
| `--context` | The build context, relative to the repository. Default: its root. |  |
| `--target` | The stage of a multi-stage Dockerfile to build. |  |
| `--build-arg` | A build argument (not a secret: it is written into the image). Repeat for several. |  |
| `--build-secret` | A secret the build mounts, read from FILE and kept in the secret store; never an argument of the build. Repeat for several. |  |
| `--container-port` | Where the process listens inside the container. Default: what the Dockerfile or the image exposes. |  |
| `--volume` | A path in the container whose data survives every deployment, such as /data. Repeat for several. |  |
| `--restart` | Docker's restart policy: no, always, unless-stopped (default) or on-failure. |  |
| `--entrypoint` | Run this program instead of the image's ENTRYPOINT: the line is split into words the way a shell would, and no shell runs it. An empty line clears the image's entrypoint (its CMD is then the program). Setting one drops the image's CMD: give --command too if it should still apply. |  |
| `--command` | Give the entrypoint these arguments instead of the image's CMD (split into words, no shell). Docker cannot clear a CMD: an empty line is refused; --clear command goes back to the image's. |  |
| `--registry-server` | The registry the account is for. Default: the image's own. |  |
| `--registry-user` | The account of a private registry. |  |
| `--registry-password-stdin` | Read the account's password from standard input. |  |
| `--remove-build-arg` | Remove a build argument. |  |
| `--remove-build-secret` | Remove a build secret, and its value. |  |
| `--remove-volume` | Stop keeping this path across deployments. The volume's data stays on the server. |  |
| `--clear` | Go back to the default of a setting: it is read from the Dockerfile or the image again. |  |
| `--clear-registry` | Remove the registry account. |  |
| `--json` | Print the settings now as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust app policy set

Change an application's policy: what you name changes, the rest stays.

```
noust app policy set [OPTIONS] DOMAIN
```

Arguments: `domain`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--password`, `--no-password` | Ask for a password. |  |
| `--realm` | The sign-in prompt's title. |  |
| `--access` | all: the password and the address list must both pass; any: either lets in. |  |
| `--allow` | Allow only these (repeat). |  |
| `--clear-allow` | Allow everyone again. |  |
| `--deny` | Refuse these (repeat). |  |
| `--clear-deny` | Refuse no one. |  |
| `--real-ip` | Read the client address from a header, believed from Cloudflare or your own proxies. |  |
| `--real-ip-header` | The header (custom): X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP... |  |
| `--trusted-proxy` | A proxy (custom). |  |
| `--rate-limit` | 10r/s or 300r/m per client address; none clears. |  |
| `--rate-burst` | Requests above the rate let through first. |  |
| `--connection-limit` | Concurrent connections per address; 0 for none. |  |
| `--header` | Send a header. |  |
| `--remove-header` | Stop sending yours. |  |
| `--hide-header` | Do not send a default. |  |
| `--hsts` | Strict-Transport-Security. |  |
| `--noindex`, `--index` | Tell search engines not to index. |  |
| `--canonical` | Serve www or the bare name, redirecting the other. |  |
| `--forward-auth-preset` | Ask an authentication service about every request, with a common service's defaults. |  |
| `--forward-auth-url` | Where each request is asked about, such as http://127.0.0.1:4180/oauth2/auth. |  |
| `--forward-auth-sign-in` | Where a visitor who is not signed in is sent (the page asked for is appended). |  |
| `--forward-auth-header` | A response header of the service to hand on to the application (repeat). |  |
| `--no-forward-auth` | Stop asking an authentication service. |  |
| `--accept-unreachable-auth` | Go ahead although the authentication service does not answer (everyone is refused until it does). |  |
| `--http3`, `--no-http3` | Serve the site over HTTP/3 (QUIC) as well (nginx 1.25 or later with the HTTP/3 module). |  |
| `--client-certs`, `--no-client-certs` | Answer only a visitor with a certificate this site's own authority signed (noust app policy clients issue makes them). |  |
| `--waf` | The web application firewall (OWASP Core Rule Set): detect writes down what the rules see, block also refuses what they score too high. |  |
| `--waf-exclude` | Leave this rule out for the site (repeat for more); replaces the list. |  |
| `--clear-waf-exclusions` | Leave no rule out for the site. |  |
| `--accept-lockout` | Go ahead although the lists refuse the address you are connected from. |  |
| `--json` | Print the policy now in force as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust app tuning set

Tune the application's unit; what is not named is kept.

```
noust app tuning set [OPTIONS] DOMAIN
```

Arguments: `domain`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--memory-high` | Soft memory limit: throttled above it, killed only at the hard one. |  |
| `--swap-max` | Swap the unit may use; 0 forbids it. |  |
| `--cpu-weight` | Share of the CPU when it is contended (100 is the default). |  |
| `--allowed-cpus` | Pin the unit to these CPUs, such as 0-3 or 0,2. |  |
| `--io-weight` | Share of the disk when it is contended. |  |
| `--nofile` | Open files (ulimit -n). |  |
| `--nproc` | Processes of the account (ulimit -u). |  |
| `--memlock` | Locked memory (ulimit -l). |  |
| `--core-dumps`, `--no-core-dumps` | Allow core dumps (ulimit -c). |  |
| `--cap` | A capability the process keeps (NET_BIND_SERVICE, ...); repeat it. Replaces the list. |  |
| `--device` | A device the process may open (/dev/nvidia0:rw, char-drm); repeat it. Replaces the list. |  |
| `--gpu` | Allow the devices a GPU needs (nvidia, dri); repeat it. |  |
| `--unset` | Remove one option (memory_high_mb, capabilities, ...); repeat it. |  |
| `--no-restart` | Write the unit but do not restart: the running process keeps what it has. |  |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Do not ask for confirmation. |  |
| `--json` | Print what was done as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

| `--clear-bind-password` | Forget its stored password. |  |
| `--user-base` | Where people are searched from, such as ou=people,dc=acme,dc=test. |  |

| `--subject-attribute` | The directory's stable id for a person: entryUUID (OpenLDAP, 389, FreeIPA) or objectGUID (Active Directory). |  |
| `--email-attribute` | Where the address is (mail). |  |
| `--name-attribute` | Where the display name is (displayName). |  |
| `--username-attribute` | Where the login name is (uid, sAMAccountName). |  |
| `--groups-attribute` | Where the entry lists its groups (memberOf). |  |
| `--group-base` | Where groups are searched, when the entry does not list them. |  |
| `--group-filter` | That search, with {dn} and {username}: (&(objectClass=groupOfNames)(member={dn})). |  |
| `--timeout` | Seconds one sign-in may take (1-30). |  |
| `--provisioning` | A first sign-in: off (an administrator links people), invite, or auto (create the account). |  |
| `--default-role` | The role of a created account. |  |
| `--default-team` | The team a created account joins ('' for the default). |  |
| `--default-team-role` | Its role there. |  |
| `--link-by-email` | Link a first sign-in to the account of its address. |  |
| `--no-link-by-email` | Never link by e-mail. |  |
| `--allowed-domain` | Only addresses of this domain (repeat). |  |
| `--clear-domains` | Allow every domain again. |  |
| `--require-email` | Refuse a person with no address. |  |
| `--no-require-email` | Let in people with no address. |  |
| `--group-sync` | Let groups decide roles and teams. |  |
| `--no-group-sync` | Stop letting groups decide. |  |
| `--map-role` | GROUP=ROLE: members get this role (repeat). |  |
| `--map-team` | GROUP=TEAM:ROLE: members join this team (repeat). |  |
| `--map-binding` | GROUP=ROLE@TEAM[/PROJECT[/ENVIRONMENT]]: members hold this role there, a built-in one on a project or a custom one anywhere (repeat). |  |
| `--clear-mappings` | Forget every group mapping. |  |
| `--json` | Print the directory as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

| Option | What it does | Default |

| `--client-id` | The client id Noust is registered as. |  |
| `--client-secret-stdin` | Read the client secret from standard input. |  |
| `--prompt-secret` | Ask for the client secret at a hidden prompt. |  |
| `--clear-secret` | Forget the stored client secret (a public client). |  |
| `--label` | What the button says after 'Sign in with'. |  |
| `--scopes` | Space separated; openid is always asked. |  |
| `--enable` | Offer it on the sign-in page. |  |
| `--disable` | Stop offering it, and refuse its answers. |  |
| `--require-email-verified` | Refuse a sign-in whose e-mail the provider does not vouch for (the default). |  |
| `--allow-unverified-email` | Let in people whose e-mail is not verified; it is then never used to find an account. |  |
| `--assume-email-verified` | Treat an e-mail the provider says nothing about as verified (Microsoft Entra, a managed directory). |  |
| `--no-assume-email-verified` | Never assume it (the default). |  |
| `--clock-skew` | Seconds of clock difference to forgive (0-300). |  |
| `--provisioning` | A first sign-in: off (an administrator links people), invite, or auto (create the account). |  |
| `--default-role` | The role of an account that provisioning creates. |  |
| `--default-team` | The team a created account joins ('' for the default team). |  |
| `--default-team-role` | Its role there. |  |
| `--link-by-email` | Link a first sign-in to the account of its verified e-mail (only one with a second factor). |  |
| `--no-link-by-email` | Never link by e-mail. |  |
| `--allowed-domain` | Only e-mail addresses of this domain (repeat for several). |  |
| `--clear-domains` | Allow every domain again. |  |
| `--require-amr` | The provider must say it used one of these methods, such as mfa (repeat for several). |  |
| `--clear-amr` | Require no method. |  |
| `--groups-claim` | Where the token lists groups; nest with '>'. |  |
| `--group-sync` | Let groups decide roles and teams at every sign-in. |  |
| `--no-group-sync` | Stop letting groups decide. |  |
| `--map-role` | GROUP=ROLE: members get this role (repeat). |  |
| `--map-team` | GROUP=TEAM:ROLE: members join this team (repeat). |  |
| `--map-binding` | GROUP=ROLE@TEAM[/PROJECT[/ENVIRONMENT]]: members hold this role there, a built-in one on a project or a custom one anywhere (repeat). |  |
| `--clear-mappings` | Forget every group mapping. |  |
| `--redirect-uri` | The callback address, when it cannot be worked out ('' to clear). |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

Arguments: `name`

On unless the backend is 'local' or backup.encrypt_new_destinations is false: a backup holds the .env and the database dumps, so it leaves this server encrypted unless you say --no-encrypt. |  |
| `--key-stdin` | Encrypt with an existing key read from standard input, as 'show-key' printed it (its text, its --json, or the two passphrases on two lines). Implies --encrypt. |  |

Subcommands: [`create`](#noust-backup-schedule-create), [`delete`](#noust-backup-schedule-delete), [`list`](#noust-backup-schedule-list), [`update`](#noust-backup-schedule-update)

### noust backup schedule create

Back an application up on a timer and drop its old scheduled backups.

```
noust backup schedule create [OPTIONS] DOMAIN
```

Arguments: `domain`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--schedule` | hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or a systemd OnCalendar expression. | `daily` |
| `--retention-count` | Keep at most this many of the backups this schedule makes (default: 7). 'default' leaves backup.max_per_app in charge, over every backup, as 2.1 did. |  |
| `--retention-days` | Delete this schedule's own backups older than this many days (default: 30). 'none' sets no age limit. |  |
| `--retention-gb` | The most the scheduled backups kept here may weigh together, in gigabytes, or 'none'. The newest always stays, whatever its size. | `none` |
| `--destination` | Push each backup to this remote destination, with its own retention. Repeatable. |  |
| `--remote-only` | Keep nothing on this server: delete each backup here once every destination holds it and its upload was checked. For a small disk; needs a --destination. |  |
| `--max-runtime` | Stop a run that takes longer than this: 90m, 2h, 1d or a number of seconds (1 minute to 7 days). No limit by default. |  |
| `--timezone` | Read the schedule in this time zone, such as Europe/Madrid (timedatectl list-timezones lists them). The server's clock by default. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

| `--json` | Print the outcome as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust create

Deploy a web application and put it online.

```
noust create [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-d`, `--domain` | Domain the application is served on. |  |
| `-s`, `--source` | Git URL, archive URL or directory to deploy from. Not with --recipe. |  |
| `--recipe` | Deploy a known application from its recipe (see 'noust recipe list'): its source, type, database and settings come from the recipe. |  |
| `--env` | Set a variable of the application environment, over --env-file and a recipe's own. Repeat for several. |  |
| `-t`, `--type` | Application type. Detected from the source when left on auto. | `auto` |
| `-p`, `--port` | Port the application listens on. A free one is chosen when omitted. |  |
| `-w`, `--webserver` | Web server that fronts the application. | `nginx` |
| `-b`, `--branch` | Git branch to deploy. |  |
| `--follow-tags` | Deploy the newest git tag that matches this glob (such as 'v*') and keep deploying new ones, from a release or a tag push, instead of following a branch. |  |
| `--no-ssl` | Serve over plain HTTP, without a certificate. |  |
| `--www` | Also answer on www.<domain>, redirecting it to the domain (see 'noust domain'). |  |
| `--env-file` | File of KEY=value lines to install as the application environment. |  |
| `--package-manager`, `--pm` | Node package manager. Detected from the lockfile when left on auto. | `auto` |
| `--subdomains` | Serve a monorepo app on this subdomain. Repeat once per app. |  |
| `--workspaces` | Deploy only this monorepo workspace. Repeat to select several. |  |
| `--no-database` | Skip database provisioning for a monorepo. |  |
| `--database` | Create a database for the application before its first build, owned by an account of its own, with its connection string in the environment (DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL for Redis). NAME defaults to one derived from the domain. Not with --recipe. |  |
| `--database-version` | The version of the --database engine, such as 17 or 11.4. The installed one when omitted; one the server does not run is refused with what it runs. |  |
| `--install-database` | Install the --database engine, in --database-version, when it is not installed. Installs packages: the same as 'noust db install'. |  |
| `--database-instance` | Make the --database on this instance Noust runs ('noust db instance list') instead of the host's engine. One is also chosen by itself when --database-version is what an instance runs and the host does not. |  |
| `--compose-file` | Compose file to use, relative to the project. Detected when omitted. |  |
| `--compose-profiles` | Activate this Docker Compose profile. Repeat to activate several. |  |
| `--layout` | Build every deploy as a release behind a health gate, or in place. Defaults to the server's deploy.layout. |  |
| `--persist` | Keep this path, relative to the app, in shared/ across releases. Repeat for several. |  |
| `--build-file` | A YAML file holding 'build:' (base_directory, install, build, start, publish_directory, runtime): the operator's block for this application, which replaces the repository's noust.yaml and is kept for every update. How several applications are deployed from one repository: see docs/build.md. |  |
| `--force` | Deploy into an app directory that already holds files: in place a git checkout is brought up to date, keeping what git does not track (.env, data), and anything else is refused, never emptied; on releases a release is added beside them. |  |
| `--no-cache` | Build the first deployment without any cache: images without their layer cache. |  |
| `--registry` | A registry account (noust registry add) to pull private images with, for a Docker Compose or container application. Repeat it for several. |  |
| `--image` | Deploy this image from a registry: name[:tag][@sha256:digest]. Needs no source. |  |
| `--builder` | How a repository becomes an image: its Dockerfile, or Railpack, which needs none (noust setup railpack). |  |
| `--dockerfile` | The Dockerfile, relative to the repository. Default: Dockerfile or Containerfile in the context. |  |
| `--context` | The build context, relative to the repository. Default: its root. |  |
| `--target` | The stage of a multi-stage Dockerfile to build. |  |
| `--build-arg` | A build argument (not a secret: it is written into the image). Repeat for several. |  |
| `--build-secret` | A secret the build mounts, read from FILE and kept in the secret store; never an argument of the build. Repeat for several. |  |
| `--container-port` | Where the process listens inside the container. Default: what the Dockerfile or the image exposes. |  |
| `--volume` | A path in the container whose data survives every deployment, such as /data. Repeat for several. |  |
| `--restart` | Docker's restart policy: no, always, unless-stopped (default) or on-failure. |  |
| `--entrypoint` | Run this program instead of the image's ENTRYPOINT: the line is split into words the way a shell would, and no shell runs it. An empty line clears the image's entrypoint (its CMD is then the program). Setting one drops the image's CMD: give --command too if it should still apply. |  |
| `--command` | Give the entrypoint these arguments instead of the image's CMD (split into words, no shell). Docker cannot clear a CMD: an empty line is refused; --clear command goes back to the image's. |  |
| `--registry-server` | The registry the account is for. Default: the image's own. |  |
| `--registry-user` | The account of a private registry. |  |
| `--registry-password-stdin` | Read the account's password from standard input. |  |
| `--team` | The team it belongs to (default: the default team). |  |
| `--project` | The project it belongs to (default: the team's default). |  |
| `--environment` | The environment it belongs to (default: production). |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |


Arguments: `database`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--engine`, `-e` | Engine the database is on. |  |
| `--all` | One policy for every database of the engine, those created later too. |  |

| `--keep-days` | Days to keep a scheduled dump here, or 'none'. | `30` |
| `--keep-gb` | The most the scheduled backups kept here may weigh together, in gigabytes, or 'none'. The newest always stays, whatever its size. | `none` |
| `--to` | Send each dump to this backup destination, keeping COUNT, DAYS and GB there. Repeatable. |  |
| `--format` | PostgreSQL's dump format. custom (pg_dump -Fc) by default. |  |
| `--verify-restore` | Load each dump into a temporary database, and drop it, as proof it restores. |  |
| `--remote-only` | Keep no copy on this server: a scheduled dump is deleted once every --to destination holds it (for a small disk). A dump that could not be sent everywhere stays. |  |
| `--disable` | Keep the settings but install no timer. |  |
| `--max-runtime` | Stop a run that takes longer than this: 90m, 2h, 1d or a number of seconds (1 minute to 7 days). No limit by default. |  |
| `--timezone` | Read the schedule in this time zone, such as Europe/Madrid (timedatectl list-timezones lists them). The server's clock by default. |  |
| `--json` | Print the policy as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust db import

Import a dump into DATABASE, creating it when it does not exist.

```
noust db import [OPTIONS] DATABASE FILE
```

Arguments: `database`, `file`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--engine`, `-e` | Engine the database is on. |  |
| `--replace` | Drop the database and load the dump into a fresh one. A safety copy is taken first and put back if the import fails. |  |
| `--keep-owners` | PostgreSQL: keep the owners and privileges the dump names. By default they are left out, because they are the roles of the server it came from, and everything belongs to the database's owner. |  |
| `--no-safety-copy` | Do not dump the database first when nothing is dropped. |  |
| `--owner` | PostgreSQL: the account a database this import makes belongs to (it must exist), instead of the default. A database that is loaded over keeps its owner. |  |
| `--as-superuser` | PostgreSQL: load the dump as the server's superuser. By default it is loaded as the database's owner, so what a dump asks beyond that (COPY ... FROM PROGRAM, extensions that need a superuser) is refused. Use it only for a dump you made or have read. Audited. |  |
| `--inspect` | Say what the file is and whether the engine can load it, and stop. |  |
| `--force`, `-f`, `-y` | Do not ask for confirmation. |  |
| `--json` | Print what the import did as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust db import-all

Import a dump of every database of an engine, and its accounts when asked.

```
noust db import-all [OPTIONS] FILE
```

Arguments: `file`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--engine`, `-e` | Engine to import into. |  |
| `--users` | Also create the accounts of the dump (PostgreSQL: its roles, with the password hash it holds). Without superuser, role-creating, replication or row-security-bypassing power, and never over an account that exists. The databases then keep the owners and privileges the dump names for those accounts. |  |
| `--accounts-file` | MySQL and MariaDB: a file of CREATE USER and GRANT statements, one per line (SHOW CREATE USER and SHOW GRANTS print them, so does pt-show-grants); mysqldump does not write the accounts. Used with --users. |  |
| `--database`, `-d` | Load only this database (repeat for several). The server's own ones (postgres) are loaded only when named. |  |
| `--replace` | Drop each database that exists and load the dump into a fresh one. A safety copy is taken first and put back if its load fails. |  |
| `--no-safety-copy` | Do not dump a database first when it is loaded over rather than replaced. |  |
| `--as-superuser` | Load every database as the server's superuser instead of as its owner. By default a database is loaded as its owner, so what a dump asks beyond that (COPY ... FROM PROGRAM, extensions that need a superuser) is refused. Use it only for a file you made or have read. Audited. |  |
| `--plan` | Say what would be created, loaded over, replaced or left out, and stop. |  |
| `--force`, `-f`, `-y` | Do not ask for confirmation. |  |
| `--json` | Print the plan or what was done as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust db instance create

Make an instance NAME and start it.

```
noust db instance create [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Arguments: `name`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--engine`, `-e` | What to run: a flavour of the catalog. |  |
| `--version` | Its version, such as 16 or 8.4 ('noust db instance catalog'). The default one when omitted. |  |
| `--memory` | Its memory limit, such as 512m or 2g. Mandatory: the container is held to it and the engine sizes its caches to it. |  |
| `--port` | The port on 127.0.0.1. A free one just above the engine's own when omitted. |  |
| `--variant` | An image of the engine with something added, such as pgvector or postgis for PostgreSQL ('noust db instance catalog'). The engine's own image when omitted. |  |
| `--init-script` | A .sql file the engine runs, in name order, the first time it starts (PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB; repeatable). It is not run again, and it is readable by the container: no secrets. |  |
| `--image` | An image of your own instead of the catalog's: repository[:tag]@sha256:DIGEST. The digest is mandatory (a tag can be moved after you looked; 'docker buildx imagetools inspect REPO:TAG' prints it) and --version says which version it is. Noust has not tested it. |  |
| `--args` | Arguments added after the ones Noust passes the engine, such as '-c max_connections=200'. Split like a shell would and never run by one. Not with --command. No secrets: a command line is visible to every local user. |  |
| `--command` | The container's whole command, instead of the engine's: Noust adds nothing to it (the memory share, TLS), so it is refused for an instance that serves TLS. Not with --args. |  |
| `--accept-untested` | Accept that Noust has not tested an image, a command or arguments you chose. Needed with --yes or --json for them; --yes alone answers the question, not this. |  |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Do not ask before making it. |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--json` | Print the instance as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

| `--plan` | Only say what it would do. |  |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Do not ask before restarting it. |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--json` | Print the settings, the plan or what was done as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

| `--json` | Print the exposure (and, with --reveal, the connection) as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|

### noust db replica

Run read replicas of this server's PostgreSQL, over TLS, with an account of their own.

```
noust db replica [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Subcommands: [`join`](#noust-db-replica-join), [`prepare`](#noust-db-replica-prepare), [`promote`](#noust-db-replica-promote), [`remove`](#noust-db-replica-remove), [`status`](#noust-db-replica-status), [`token`](#noust-db-replica-token)

### noust db replica join

Make this server a replica of the primary CODE names.

```
noust db replica join [OPTIONS] [CODE]
```

Arguments: `code`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--token-file` | Read the join code from this file. |  |
| `--replace-data` | Accept that this server's PostgreSQL data is replaced by the primary's. |  |
| `--discard-previous` | Delete this server's old data directory once the replica streams (it is kept otherwise). |  |
| `--plan` | Check everything and say what would be done. |  |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust db replica prepare

Make room for a replica called NAME on this server, and print its join code.

```
noust db replica prepare [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Arguments: `name`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--engine`, `-e` | The engine: postgresql, or mysql for MySQL and MariaDB. | `postgresql` |
| `--from` | Where the replica connects from: its address or network (203.0.113.7, 10.0.0.0/24). |  |
| `--host` | The name the replica connects to. PostgreSQL's certificate must cover it. |  |
| `--listen` | Make PostgreSQL listen here too (an address of this server, or '*'). Needed when it listens on the loopback only; restarts it once. |  |
| `--ca-file` | The authority that signed PostgreSQL's certificate, when the replica does not trust it already (a private authority). |  |
| `--open-firewall` | Allow the port from the replica's address. |  |
| `--token-file` | Write the join code to this file (0600) instead of printing it. |  |
| `--plan` | Check everything and say what would be done. |  |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Do not ask before restarting PostgreSQL. |  |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

FROM PROGRAM) with that account: use it only for a dump you made or have read, when the error says the owner may not do what it asks. Audited. |  |

### noust db transfer

Move DATABASE from one server of the fleet to another.

```
noust db transfer [OPTIONS] DATABASE
```

Arguments: `database`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--engine`, `-e` | The engine it is on at the source: postgresql, mysql (MariaDB too) or mongodb, or an instance such as postgresql@pg16. | `postgresql` |
| `--from` | The server that holds the database. |  |
| `--to` | The server that receives it. |  |
| `--to-engine` | The engine or instance on the target, when it is not the source's own. |  |
| `--as` | Its name on the target; the same by default. |  |
| `--replace` | Replace a database of that name the target holds, after a safety copy of it taken there. |  |
| `--accounts` | Also make the accounts with access to it, with the password the source holds for each and the profile they had. The passwords pass through this machine and are kept nowhere. |  |
| `--drop-source` | Drop it from the source once it has moved, after a last dump kept there. Refused while an application uses it. |  |
| `--plan` | Only show what would happen. |  |

### noust fleet authorize

Let a central manage this server, and print the join code for it.

```

```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--central-key` | The central's public key line for this server, as 'noust node key' printed it. |  |
| `--name` | The central's name. |  |
| `--ssh-user` | Account the central's tunnel logs in as. The default is created and restricted in sshd; root needs --i-understand. | `noust-tunnel` |
| `--i-understand` | Confirm --ssh-user root: a key in root's authorized_keys can create Unix sockets as root, however it is restricted. |  |
| `--replace-root-key` | A central's old public key to take out of root's authorized_keys once the new line is in place, whatever its comment (a 0600 copy of the file is kept). 'noust node migrate-tunnel' prints it for a node a 3.0 central authorized as root. |  |
| `--access` | The most any central may do on this server: read, deploy (operate and update applications) or admin. Unchanged when omitted (admin on a server that never set it). |  |
| `--allow-host-access`, `--no-host-access` | Let centrals reach the host itself: change how this server is reached (SSH keys, sshd, firewall, accounts) and make root-equivalent changes (raw units, cron commands, backup hooks, raw site configuration), on top of --access admin. Off unless set. |  |
| `--allow-self` | Authorize even though this server looks like the central that issued the key (testing only). |  |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Replace an older token and move a background console to a service without asking. |  |
| `--json` | Print the result, join code included, as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust fleet enroll

Enroll the server at --host as NAME: install Noust if needed, authorize this central, join it.

```
noust fleet enroll [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Arguments: `name`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` | The server's address or name. |  |
| `--port` | Where its sshd listens. | `22` |
| `--ssh-user` | The account the credential is for: root, or an account with passwordless sudo. | `root` |
| `--key-file` | A private key to log in with instead of a password. It is read, used once and forgotten. |  |
| `--ask-passphrase` | The key has a passphrase: ask for it, without echo. |  |
| `--password-stdin` | Read the password from one line of standard input instead of asking for it. |  |
| `--host-key-fingerprint` | The server's ed25519 host key fingerprint, confirmed some other way (the provider's console, ssh-keygen -lf on the server). Without it the fingerprint is shown and asked. |  |
| `--access` | The most this central may do on the server. | `admin` |
| `--allow-host-access`, `--no-host-access` | Also let this central reach the host itself there (SSH keys, sshd, the firewall). |  |
| `--no-install` | Do not install Noust on the server: fail when it is not there. |  |

### noust import


Arguments: `path`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--from` | The platform whose configuration the repository carries, or whose server to read (coolify, dokploy: with --url). |  |
| `--url` | coolify and dokploy: the server's address, https://coolify.example.com. |  |
| `--token-file` | coolify and dokploy: a file whose first line is a read-only API token (or set NOUST_IMPORT_TOKEN). |  |
| `--app` | coolify and dokploy: the application to read, by name or id. Without it they are listed. |  |
| `--deploy` | Deploy it on this domain with the proposal, through the normal create path. |  |
| `--source` | With --deploy: the repository to deploy. Default: PATH itself. |  |
| `--branch` | With --deploy: the branch to deploy. |  |
| `--env-file` | With --deploy: NAME=value lines, for the variables the platform kept. |  |
| `--env` | With --deploy: a variable's value. Repeat for several. |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--json` | Print the proposal (or, with --deploy, what was done) as JSON. |  |

### noust notify channel set

Create or change a channel, keeping what is not mentioned.

```
noust notify channel set [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Arguments: `name`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--type` | The channel's type. |  |
| `--enable`, `--disable` | Turn the channel on or off. |  |
| `--set` | A setting of the type (chat_id, device, mention_role_id...). Not a credential. |  |
| `--secret` | Ask for a credential (webhook_url, bot_token, user_key...), hidden. |  |
| `--secret-stdin` | Read one credential from standard input. |  |
| `--event` | This channel's own switch for an event (see 'noust notify events'). |  |
| `--clear-events` | Forget this channel's own event switches. |  |
| `--route-app` | Only this application (a * pattern works). |  |
| `--route-project` | Only this project. |  |
| `--route-environment` | Only this environment (or project/environment). |  |
| `--route-tag` | Only applications with this tag. |  |
| `--min-severity` | Skip everything below this severity. |  |
| `--server-events`, `--no-server-events` | With a route: also hear what is about the server, not an application. |  |
| `--clear-route` | Remove the channel's route. |  |
| `--quiet` | Quiet hours, such as 22:00-07:00. |  |
| `--quiet-timezone` | The time zone of the quiet hours (UTC by default). |  |
| `--quiet-allow` | The lowest severity that still gets through the quiet hours (failed by default). |  |
| `--no-digest` | Deliver what the quiet hours held one by one. |  |
| `--clear-quiet` | Remove the channel's quiet hours. |  |
| `--flood` | At most MAX messages in any MINUTES minutes, such as 20/10; the rest arrive as one. |  |
| `--clear-flood` | Remove the channel's anti-flood cap. |  |
| `--summary-at` | Send everything below --summary-below once a day at this time, as one message. |  |
| `--summary-timezone` | The time zone of the summary. |  |
| `--summary-below` | What waits for the summary: what is below this severity (warning by default). |  |
| `--summary-days` | The days it goes out on, such as mon,wed,fri (every day by default). |  |
| `--clear-summary` | Remove the channel's summary. |  |
| `--team` | Make it the channel of this team: it hears only that team's applications. NAME is then what the team calls it. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust preview enable

Turn previews on for an application, or change their settings.

```
noust preview enable [OPTIONS] DOMAIN
```

Arguments: `domain`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--domain` | Base domain previews answer under; *.BASE must point at this server. Required to turn previews on; kept when changing other settings. |  |
| `--max` | How many previews may exist at once (1 to 20). [default: 3, or the current value] |  |
| `--ttl` | How long a preview lives without a push: 12h, 7d, 2w (1 hour to 90 days). [default: 7d, or the current value] |  |
| `--allow-bots`, `--no-allow-bots` | Build previews of pull requests opened or pushed to by bot accounts (Dependabot, Renovate). [default: no, or the current value] |  |
| `--exclude-env` | A variable never copied to previews; repeat for more. Replaces the current list; existing previews lose them at their next push. |  |
| `--no-exclude-env` | Copy every variable again (clear the excluded list). |  |
| `--env-mode` | Which of the application's variables a preview is given: 'allowlist' (only --allow-env, the default for previews turned on now) or 'all' (every one less --exclude-env, as before 3.4). |  |
| `--allow-env` | A variable an 'allowlist' preview copies; repeat for more. Replaces the current list. |  |
| `--no-allow-env` | Copy no variable of the application's (clear the allowed list). |  |
| `--data` | 'empty' gives each preview a database of its own, 'clone' a database of its own that starts as a copy of the application's, 'shared' lets it use the application's (a pull request can then write into production's). Default for previews turned on now: empty, when the application has a database. |  |
| `--domain-template` | How a preview is named, such as '{{pr_id}}-{{name}}.{{base}}' ({{pr_id}}, {{random}}, {{domain}}, {{name}}, {{base}}); '' goes back to pr-<n>-<name>.BASE. Applies to the previews made from now on. |  |
| `--noindex`, `--index` | Tell search engines to leave previews alone (X-Robots-Tag). [default: noindex] |  |
| `--forks` | 'refuse' (a pull request from a fork, or from someone not trusted with the repository, gets no preview) or 'approve' (it waits for an operator to approve each commit: noust preview approve). [default: refuse] |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--json` | Print the settings as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

| `--var` | Give a variable a value: the ones the recipe requires, or any it sets. Repeat for several. |  |
| `--var-file` | A file of NAME=VALUE lines, under --var. |  |
| `--port` | The port to listen on; a free one is chosen when omitted. |  |
| `--no-ssl` | Do not request a certificate. |  |
| `--www` | Also answer on www.<domain>, as a redirect. |  |
| `--force` | Deploy into an application directory that already holds files. |  |
| `--no-backups` | Do not schedule the daily backups an installed application starts with. |  |
| `--install-requirements` | Install the language runtime and the database engines the recipe needs and this server lacks, instead of stopping. |  |
| `--database` | The SQL engine to run it on, for a recipe that offers a choice (WordPress runs on either). |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust restore-server

Bring a whole server back from a bundle of Noust's own state.

```
noust restore-server [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--from` | The bundle: a path, or its name on this server. |  |
| `--from-destination` | Fetch the bundle from this backup destination first (with --name). |  |
| `--name` | With --from-destination: the bundle's name there. |  |
| `--host` | With --from-destination: the old server's folder there. |  |
| `--app` | Restore only this application. Repeatable. |  |
| `--skip` | Leave this application out. Repeatable. |  |
| `--skip-state` | Noust's state is already back (a run that stopped): only bring the applications up. |  |
| `--force` | Restore over a server that already holds state. |  |
| `--install` | Install what this machine lacks: the web server, Docker (when an application or an instance needs it) and the database engines. Without it nothing is installed. |  |
| `--no-databases` | Do not bring back the databases no application owns. |  |
| `--accept-schema-changes` | Restore an application's files even past a schema change nothing restores the database for. |  |
| `--plan` | Say what the bundle would bring back, and stop. Changes nothing. |  |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Do not ask for confirmation. |  |
| `--passphrase-file` | Read the bundle's passphrase from this file (mode 600). |  |
| `--json` | Print the report as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust token create

Issue a named, scoped API token. NAME must be unique across every token     ever issued, live or revoked.

```
noust token create [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Arguments: `name`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--scope` | What the token may do. | `read` |
| `--expires-hours` | Lifetime in hours. Omitted: the token only dies by revocation. |  |
| `--owner` | Account the token acts for, with at most its role. Required under the ENS profile. |  |
| `--permission` | Narrow the token to this permission (repeat). The owner must hold it. |  |
| `--team` | Bind the token to this team: it sees nothing else (needs --owner). |  |
| `--project` | Bind it to this project of the team. |  |

### noust update

Pull the latest code, rebuild and restart an application.

```
noust update [OPTIONS] DOMAIN
```

Arguments: `domain`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-s`, `--source` | Fetch from this source instead of the recorded one. |  |
| `-b`, `--branch` | Git branch to update from. |  |
| `--commit` | Deploy this commit (full or abbreviated) instead of the head of the branch. |  |
| `--tag` | Deploy the commit this tag points at. Never an older tag than one already deployed: use 'noust rollback' for that. |  |
| `--package-manager`, `--pm` | Node package manager. Detected from the lockfile when left on auto. | `auto` |
| `-y`, `--force` | Rebuild without asking when the branch has nothing new since the live commit. |  |
| `--schema-changed-ok` | With --commit, go back even past deployments that changed the database schema. |  |
| `--no-cache` | Build from scratch: empty the build cache first, install the dependencies again instead of taking them from the release that serves, and build images without their layer cache. Rebuilds what is live even when there is nothing new. |  |
| `--during-freeze` | Deploy although deploys are frozen for the application (noust deploy freeze). A person's decision, recorded in the audit trail. |  |
| `--build-only` | Build the release and leave it waiting, not serving: nothing is activated, no hook runs and nothing restarts. Make it serve later, without building it again, with 'noust releases promote'. Only for an application on the releases layout. |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust web enable

Run the panel as a systemd service that survives reboots.

```
noust web enable [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-H`, `--host` | Interface to bind to. Anything but loopback needs TLS (--tls-cert/--tls-key or --self-signed) or --insecure-http. | `127.0.0.1` |
| `-p`, `--port` | Port to listen on. | `8080` |
| `--require-https` | Serve TLS from the panel and refuse cleartext. Needs --tls-cert and --tls-key, or --self-signed. |  |
| `--tls-cert` | Certificate chain to serve. |  |
| `--tls-key` | Private key for the certificate. |  |
| `--self-signed` | Serve TLS with a self-signed certificate, minted under /etc/noust/panel-tls and reused while it is valid. |  |
| `--insecure-http` | Serve cleartext HTTP beyond loopback. The access token and the session cookie cross the network unencrypted. |  |
| `--allow-ip` | Only answer this address or network. Repeat to allow several. Restricts who connects; encrypts nothing. |  |
| `--trusted-proxy` | Believe forwarding headers from this peer. Declare the proxy that terminates TLS so the session cookie is issued with Secure. |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

| `--trusted-proxy` | Believe forwarding headers from this peer. Declare the proxy that terminates TLS so the session cookie is issued with Secure. |  |
| `-d`, `--daemon` | Run in the background, until 'noust web stop' or the next reboot. 'noust web enable' survives reboots. |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust web start

Start the panel and print an access token.

```
noust web start [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-H`, `--host` | Interface to bind to. Anything but loopback needs TLS (--tls-cert/--tls-key or --self-signed) or --insecure-http. | `127.0.0.1` |
| `-p`, `--port` | Port to listen on. | `8080` |
| `--require-https` | Serve TLS from the panel and refuse cleartext. Needs --tls-cert and --tls-key, or --self-signed. |  |
| `--tls-cert` | Certificate chain to serve. |  |
| `--tls-key` | Private key for the certificate. |  |
| `--self-signed` | Serve TLS with a self-signed certificate, minted under /etc/noust/panel-tls and reused while it is valid. |  |
| `--insecure-http` | Serve cleartext HTTP beyond loopback. The access token and the session cookie cross the network unencrypted. |  |
| `--allow-ip` | Only answer this address or network. Repeat to allow several. Restricts who connects; encrypts nothing. |  |
| `--trusted-proxy` | Believe forwarding headers from this peer. Declare the proxy that terminates TLS so the session cookie is issued with Secure. |  |
| `-d`, `--daemon` | Run in the background, until 'noust web stop' or the next reboot. 'noust web enable' survives reboots. |  |
| `--under-systemd` | Run as noust-web.service does: print no token, write no PID file. Written into the unit by 'noust web enable'; not for interactive use. |  |
| `--keep-token` | With --daemon: serve the access token already issued and print none. How 'noust fleet authorize' puts a background console back; not for interactive use. |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

```
noust web status [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |

| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust web token

Show the state of the access token, or issue a new one with --new.

```
noust web token [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--new`, `--rotate` | Issue a new access token. The token currently in use stops working. |  |
| `-r`, `--regenerate` | Issue a new token and rotate the signing key, logging out every open session and invalidating every API token and TOTP backup code. |  |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Do not ask for confirmation. |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust workspace

A monorepo as one application per workspace.

```
noust workspace [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Subcommands: [`create`](#noust-workspace-create), [`detect`](#noust-workspace-detect)

### noust workspace create

Deploy workspaces of a monorepo, one application each.

```
noust workspace create [OPTIONS] SOURCE
```

Arguments: `source`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--app` | A workspace (its name or its directory) and the domain to deploy it on. Repeat. |  |
| `--branch` | The branch to deploy; the repository's default otherwise. |  |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Do not ask before applying what a plan runs as root (cron jobs, previews). |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show the detail of each step. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Rehearse without changing anything. Read-only checks still run. |  |
| `--no-color` | Never emit colour. |  |
| `--json` | Print each application's plan and result as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |

### noust workspace detect

Find the workspaces of a repository and which of them are applications.

```
noust workspace detect [OPTIONS] SOURCE
```

Arguments: `source`

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--branch` | The branch to read; the repository's default otherwise. |  |
| `--json` | Print the workspaces as JSON. |  |
| `--reason` | Why this change is made (a change reference, a ticket). Recorded with the command in the audit log; required only where a compliance framework asks for it (ENS) or security.change_reasons is on. |  |
